correctness.rationale: For fixed m and finite k, every connected k-set in C_n^m has boundary at least m(m+1), with equality exactly on m-cliques (k=m) or cyclic k-intervals (k>m); every other cut differs by >=2 edges. O(n q^(B+2)) excludes other candidates; O(n q^(B+1)) excludes failed internal connectivity. Distinct cutsets cannot coincide (connected-host symmetric-difference argument), and any dependent pair requires an additional deletion, so all joint factorial moments converge to the claimed independent Poisson values. Exact checker enumerated 95879 local configurations/assertions; the proof itself covers all n sufficiently large and all fixed m.

value.rationale: The finite-size hierarchy answers a natural subproblem of the explicitly posed small-bandwidth percolation direction. The uncommon transition from m-clique components to interval components creates one exceptional intensity and a flat sequence of intensities at every higher fixed size. This identifies a natural limiting law for a canonical random-graph observable, not a tabular recomputation.
